What is CSS?: CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) controls the visual presentation of HTML. Rules consist of a selector and a declaration block with properties and values. Apply via inline, internal (<style>), or external (.css file).
Selectors: CSS selectors target elements: element (p), class (.my-class), id (#my-id), attribute ([type="text"]), universal (*). Combinators: descendant (div p), child (div > p), sibling (h2 + p).
Colors & Units: Color formats: named (red), hex (#FF5733), RGB (rgb(255, 87, 51)), RGBA (rgba(255, 87, 51, 0.5)), HSL/HSLA. Units: px, em (relative to parent font), rem (relative to root), %, vw/vh, ch.
Typography: Typography properties: font-family, font-size, font-weight (100-900), font-style, text-align, text-decoration, text-transform, line-height, letter-spacing. Use web fonts via @font-face or Google Fonts.
Box Model: Every element is a box: content (inner), padding (around content), border (edge), margin (outside). Use box-sizing: border-box to include padding/border in width.
CSS Variables: CSS custom properties (variables) defined with --name, accessed with var(--name). They cascade and can be overridden, enabling easy theme systems.
Specificity & Cascade: CSS specificity determines which rule wins. Inline > ID > Class > Element. When equal, last rule wins. Use !important sparingly — it breaks the natural cascade.
Inheritance: Some CSS properties inherit from parent elements: color, font-family, line-height. Others like margin, padding, border do not. Control with inherit, initial, unset, revert.
Cascade Layers Intro: The @layer rule defines cascade layers. Styles in later layers override earlier ones regardless of specificity. Use to organize resets, base styles, components, and utilities in predictable order.
CSS Reset & Normalize: Browsers apply default styles inconsistently. CSS resets remove all defaults (margin: 0, padding: 0). Normalize.css preserves useful defaults while fixing cross-browser differences. Choose based on project needs.

Display Property: The display property controls rendering: block (full width, new line), inline (flows with text), inline-block (inline but accepts width/height), none (hidden, removed from flow). Modern: flex, grid.
Flexbox: Flexbox is a 1D layout model. Container: display: flex. Main axis: justify-content. Cross axis: align-items. Items wrap with flex-wrap, grow with flex-grow, order with order.
CSS Grid: CSS Grid is a 2D layout system. Define columns with grid-template-columns, rows with grid-template-rows. Use grid-area with named template areas for complex layouts.
Positioning: position values: static (default), relative (offset from normal), absolute (relative to positioned ancestor), fixed (relative to viewport), sticky (toggles between relative/fixed on scroll).
Responsive Design: Media queries adapt layouts to screen sizes. Use @media (min-width: ...) for mobile-first approach. Common breakpoints: 576px (mobile), 768px (tablet), 992px (desktop), 1200px (wide).
Backgrounds & Gradients: Background properties: background-color, background-image, background-size, background-position, background-repeat. Gradients: linear-gradient() and radial-gradient(). Multiple backgrounds can be layered.
Animations: CSS animations use @keyframes to define sequences. The animation shorthand: name, duration, timing function, delay, iteration count, direction, fill mode.
List Styling & Counters: Style lists with list-style-type, list-style-position, list-style-image. CSS counters (counter-reset, counter-increment) create numbered headings, table-of-contents, or custom list numbering.
Form Styling with CSS: Style form elements using CSS: inputs, textareas, selects, checkboxes, radio buttons, and buttons. Normalize browser defaults. Use :focus, :valid, :invalid, :disabled pseudo-classes for state styling.

Box Shadows: The box-shadow property adds shadows: offset-x offset-y blur-radius spread-radius color. Multiple shadows can be layered. Use inset for inner shadows.
Text Effects: Text styling: text-shadow for shadows, text-overflow for ellipsis, word-break for breaking long words, white-space for spacing control, text-wrap for wrapping behavior.
Filters & Blend Modes: CSS filter applies visual effects: blur(), brightness(), contrast(), grayscale(), sepia(), hue-rotate(), drop-shadow(). mix-blend-mode blends elements with their background.
Clip Path & Shapes: clip-path clips elements to a shape: circle(), ellipse(), polygon(), inset(). shape-outside makes text wrap around a shape.
Object Fit & Position: object-fit controls how replaced elements (images, videos) fit their container: fill, contain, cover, none, scale-down. object-position sets alignment within the box.
Overflow & Scroll: overflow controls content overflow: visible, hidden, scroll, auto. overflow-x/overflow-y for axis-specific. scroll-behavior: smooth for smooth scrolling. scroll-snap for snap points.
Cursor & Pointer Events: The cursor property changes the mouse cursor: pointer, grab, text, not-allowed, wait. pointer-events controls click/touch behavior: auto (default), none (disable), visiblePainted (SVG).
Resize & Object View: The resize property makes elements user-resizable: both, horizontal, vertical. field-sizing makes textareas/contenteditable auto-size. object-view-box crops replaced elements without changing the image.
Columns & Multi-Column: Multi-column layout with column-count, column-width, column-gap, column-rule. Content flows automatically between columns. Useful for text-heavy layouts like newspapers.

CSS Architecture (BEM): Scalable CSS methodologies: BEM (Block Element Modifier) uses naming like .block__element--modifier. Prevents conflicts and improves maintainability by enforcing naming conventions.
Preprocessors (Sass/SCSS): CSS preprocessors extend CSS with variables, nesting, mixins, functions. SCSS features: $variables, @mixin/@include, & parent selector, built-in functions for colors and math.
CSS Layers (@layer): The @layer rule controls cascade layer order. Later layers override earlier ones regardless of specificity. Useful for organizing resets, components, and utilities.
Container Queries: Container queries (@container) style elements based on container size rather than viewport. Define a containment context with container-type. Enables truly reusable components.
Nesting & @scope: CSS nesting (native) lets you nest selectors like SCSS. The @scope rule limits styles to a subtree, providing better encapsulation without Shadow DOM.
Logical Properties: Logical properties use flow-relative directions: margin-inline-start instead of margin-left, padding-block instead of padding-top/padding-bottom. Better for internationalization and RTL support.
CSS Functions: Powerful CSS functions: calc() for math, min()/max()/clamp() for responsive values, attr() for HTML attributes, url() for resources, var() for variables.
Content Visibility: content-visibility skips rendering of off-screen elements for performance. contain isolates layout/style/paint. content-visibility: auto automatically skips hidden content.
CSS Color Modern Functions: Modern CSS color functions: color-mix() blends colors, color() accesses wider gamuts (Display P3, sRGB), lch()/lab() for perceptually uniform colors, oklch()/oklab() for better gradients.
@property & Custom Properties Deep Dive: The @property rule defines typed CSS custom properties with initial values and inheritance control. Enables animation of custom properties, validation, and better developer ergonomics.
Container Query Units & Style Queries: Container query units: cqw (1% container width), cqh (1% height), cqi (1% inline size), cqb (1% block size), cqmin/cqmax. Style queries (@container style()) query computed style values.
View Transitions API: View Transitions animate between page states or navigations. Use @view-transition navigation rule, view-transition-name on elements, and ::view-transition-* pseudo-elements for custom animations.

CSS Methodologies: Beyond BEM: SMACSS (categorizes into base/layout/module/state/theme), ITCSS (layers by specificity), OOCSS (separates structure from skin, container from content). Choose what fits your project.
PostCSS & Autoprefixer: PostCSS is a tool for transforming CSS with JavaScript plugins. Autoprefixer automatically adds vendor prefixes (-webkit-, -moz-, etc.). Other plugins enable future CSS syntax today.
Tailwind CSS & Utility-First: Utility-first CSS uses small, composable classes. Tailwind CSS provides .flex, .text-center, .p-4 etc. Encourages design consistency and reduces CSS file size. Trade-off: verbose HTML.

CSS Modules & Scoped Styles: CSS Modules generate locally scoped class names. Imported like JS modules. Class names are hashed at build time to avoid conflicts. Works well with component frameworks like React, Vue, Svelte.
CSS Grid Advanced: Advanced Grid: subgrid passes grid tracks to children. auto-fill/auto-fit for responsive grids without media queries. grid-auto-flow: dense fills gaps automatically.
Performance & Best Practices: CSS performance: minimize specificity chains, avoid expensive properties (box-shadow, border-radius), use will-change sparingly, avoid @import, reduce repaints/reflows, use GPU-accelerated properties (transform, opacity).
CSS Debugging & DevTools: Browser DevTools: inspect computed styles, trace specificity, toggle pseudo-classes (:hover, :focus), edit live CSS, view box model diagram, debug animations with timeline. Use outline to visualize elements.
Print & Accessibility Styles: Print stylesheets optimize pages for paper: hide nav/sidebars/ads, use page-break-* properties, ensure link URLs print. Accessibility: respect prefers-reduced-motion, prefers-color-scheme, prefers-contrast, forced-colors.

CSS Grid Advanced: CSS Grid Layout is a two-dimensional layout system. Key properties: grid-template-columns and grid-template-rows define tracks. fr unit distributes available space. grid-template-areas provides visual layout mapping. auto-fit and auto-fill create responsive grids without media queries. minmax() sets flexible track sizes. gap controls gutter spacing. Grid placement functions: grid-column, grid-row, grid-area. Grid is best for page-level layouts and two-dimensional arrangements.
CSS Custom Properties (Variables): CSS Custom Properties (CSS variables) enable reusable values throughout a stylesheet. Declared with --name and accessed with var(--name, fallback). They cascade like regular CSS — set global variables on :root and override in specific scopes. CSS variables can be changed at runtime via JavaScript (element.style.setProperty('--color', 'red')) enabling dynamic theming. Use with calc() for computed values. Unlike preprocessor variables (Sass/Less), CSS variables cascade and can be updated dynamically.
CSS Animations & Keyframes: CSS animations bring interfaces to life. @keyframes defines animation steps using percentage points or from/to. The animation shorthand: name, duration, timing function, delay, iteration count, direction, fill mode, play state. Timing functions: ease, linear, ease-in, ease-out, ease-in-out, cubic-bezier(), steps(). animation-fill-mode: forwards retains the end state. animation-direction: alternate creates smooth back-and-forth animations. prefers-reduced-motion respects user accessibility settings.
CSS Transforms & Transitions: CSS transform modifies element appearance: translate() (move), rotate() (turn), scale() (size), skew() (shear). transform-origin changes the pivot point. 3D transforms: translateZ(), rotateX(), rotateY(), perspective(). backface-visibility: hidden prevents reverse-side rendering. transition animates property changes smoothly with duration, timing function, and delay. Use will-change to hint at upcoming transforms for GPU acceleration. Hardware-accelerated properties: transform, opacity.
CSS Container Queries: Container queries allow styling elements based on their container's size rather than the viewport. Define a containment context with container-type: inline-size and optionally name it with container-name. Use @container (min-width: 400px) to apply styles when the container reaches that width. Container queries are ideal for reusable component libraries where a component must adapt to various placement contexts. They work with cqw, cqi (container query units).

BEM Methodology: Block Element Modifier (BEM) is a naming convention that makes CSS more maintainable. Block: standalone component (.card). Element: part of a block (.card__title). Modifier: variant (.card--featured, .card__title--large). Benefits: prevents naming conflicts, increases readability, and creates a clear relationship between HTML and CSS. Each selector has the same specificity, making overrides predictable. Works well with preprocessors using & nesting.
CSS Preprocessors (Sass/PostCSS): CSS preprocessors extend CSS with features like variables, nesting, mixins, functions, and inheritance. Sass/SCSS is the most popular: $variables, @mixin/@include for reusable styles, @extend for inheritance, nesting for hierarchy, & parent selector, and built-in functions (darken, lighten, rgba). PostCSS is a tool for transforming CSS with plugins: Autoprefixer (adds vendor prefixes), PostCSS Preset Env (future CSS syntax), CSS Modules (local scoping). Modern browsers support many features (CSS variables, nesting via postcss-nesting) reducing preprocessor dependency. Consider native CSS vs preprocessed CSS based on team preferences and project needs.
